_doc: Unaided concept-query recall against the verified search test set. The metric: does a query built from the topic's REGISTERED P/I/C/design (with drug-class expansion) retrieve a trial's PMID WITHOUT being told the PMID? Scored ONLY over SOURCE_VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE entries (docs/search_test_set.json). The current per-topic pubmed_queries are enumerated <uid>[uid] lists (a hardcoded PMID set that discovers nothing new), so the baseline is 0 of 6. The concept-query engine (scripts/search_rebuild.py) uses class-term expansion (GLP-1 receptor agonist -> semaglutide/dulaglutide/...; mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist -> spironolactone/eplerenone/...) and PAGINATION over the full boolean result set (never a top-N relevance cut).
improvement_provenance: recall rose because the QUERY improved (concept + class expansion + pagination), NOT because the test set grew or a verification state was loosened; the denominator is the same 6 SOURCE_VERIFIED_ELIGIBLE trials. The one apparent miss during measurement (TECOS) was a wrong target PMID in the harness (26105174, a cardiomyopathy case report) corrected to the real TECOS PMID 26052984 -- a harness error, not a search failure or a test-set change.

results.via: MRA class -> eplerenone AND HFrEF AND RCT
sitagliptin AND type 2 diabetes AND RCT
DPP-4 class -> omarigliptin AND type 2 diabetes AND RCT
GLP-1 class -> semaglutide AND type 2 diabetes AND RCT

scope: This is a RETRIEVAL-recall measurement of the concept-query engine. It is not yet wired into the pipeline's fetch (that corpus-moving integration is the delicate step, done behind a full 32-topic before/after). A better query pointed at the wrong eligibility universe is still the wrong universe: retrieval is necessary, not sufficient -- each retrieved trial still passes screening + source-verified extraction before it can pool.
